_comment: A row-major cavalry squadron standing under bow fire closes up over its casualties instead of reflowing by roster order. uid 0: 42 mounts on 7 files (6 full ranks; 40 wu files, 120 wu ranks), facing north at (700, 640), with a morale floor of 50 under fire so it holds. uid 1: 60 Archers at (700, 200) facing south, their reach stretched to 460 wu; they shoot the squadron's front ranks from tick 160 on. Volleys land at tick 162 (42 -> 40) and tick 282 (40 -> 37). slots_across_centreline and slot_lateral_excess are read from the full dump on the volley's own tick, before the mounts move (DemoDefects.derived_field). On the merge-base (e81ea9fa) the identity layout renumbers every cell behind each fallen mount, so at tick 162 15 mounts get a slot across the squadron's centreline and one is sent 200 wu (five files) sideways of his place; at tick 282, 18 and 154.7 wu. Here none is sent across, and none more than one file pitch sideways: 40.0 wu at tick 162 (pinned at a pitch plus a 0.5 wu float margin) and 41.0 wu at tick 282 (pinned at 41.5: the bodies stood up to 0.8 wu off their slots at tick 280, before that volley). The squadron's centre stays within 3 wu of x = 700 through tick 420 here; on the merge-base the torn block drags it to x = 639.38 by tick 420. Both trees also drift the squadron rearward (south), 88.6 wu here and 103.5 wu on the merge-base by tick 420, a separate pre-existing effect. all_teams_control and drill keep both sides under test control. Each slots_across_centreline, slot_lateral_excess and tick-420 position pin fails on the merge-base.
